version.changelog: Compact claim links (/c/<token>): claim URLs are now short enough that agents have no reason to truncate them. Explicit instruction: share claimUrl byte-for-byte, never shorten or replace any part with '...'. Claim page now validates links before sign-in.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly a disclosed here.now publishing helper, but it also persists API keys and exposes broad Drive/account management features that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Network upload and file reads are expected for publishing and Drive import/export, and the scripts operate on user-specified paths rather than crawling the whole filesystem; however Drive operations can move private content to cloud storage.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install instruction uses an npx-based skills add command from heredotnow/skill; the inspected artifact itself contains only markdown plus two shell helpers and no hidden install-time persistence mechanism.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger language includes broad phrases such as sharing, putting online, and generating a URL; publishing defaults to anyone-with-link access for personal sites, so accidental invocation could expose selected content if the agent does not confirm scope and access mode.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs agents to save returned API keys to ~/.herenow/credentials without asking the user to perform the step, and publish state stores claim tokens in .herenow/state.json. The credentials file is chmod 600 and disclosed, but it creates durable account access.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Publishing selected files or folders to here.now is coherent with the stated purpose, but the body also covers private Drive storage, scoped token sharing, deletion/revocation, profiles, domains, variables, proxy routes, and other account operations that are not prominent in the top-level description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to publish selected files to here.now and potentially manage here.now Drive and site/account settings. Confirm exactly which files will be uploaded, whether the site will be public, password-protected, or restricted, and whether API keys should be stored in ~/.herenow/credentials. Review and rotate/revoke tokens if you stop using the skill.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in part: Drive storage, token sharing, deletion, and account-management references are real artifact-backed capabilities, but they are described in the body rather than hidden; the concern is under-disclosure in the top-level framing.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted as a Review concern: persistent API key storage is disclosed and useful for permanent publishing, but instructing the agent to save the key itself creates durable account access.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: private Drive storage and share-token handoff are real capabilities and can be broad, including full-Drive access when pathPrefix is null; the skill does recommend narrow prefixes and short TTLs.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: broader profile, domain, variable, proxy, delete, and analytics operations are referenced through docs and may mutate account assets; they are not implemented as hidden script behavior but expand the skill's effective scope.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: the trigger phrases are broad for a skill that can publish content to externally reachable URLs.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted in part: public-link publishing is core to the skill and is disclosed, but the manifest does not require an upfront confirmation of selected content and access mode.
[E1] expected: Downgraded: uploading to an API-returned uploadUrl is expected for this publishing/storage flow, and credentials are not sent on that PUT; the residual risk is lack of URL validation if the service response is compromised or redirected.
[E1] expected: Downgraded: finalizeUrl comes from the here.now create/update response and the script blocks authenticated non-default base URLs unless explicitly overridden; still, the finalize URL itself is not independently validated before sending authenticated finalize data.
